sections.title: Layers (Wave A)
sections.note: General Planner layer rework — useful with or without a stack.

questions.q: Sub-layer drag/RCO onto another layer: what happens?
questions.why: Your text says the two layers' sub-layers change place. Moving one way is also useful.

opts.t: Drag = swap, Ctrl+drag = move; menu offers both
opts.d: Swap is the default gesture, as written.
Move is the more common operation in Photoshop terms.

questions.q: Which sub-layer rows show under a layer?
questions.why: Your 9 + windows, plus floors, roofs, notes, legacy cables, marks, traces = 16 rows.

opts.t: Your 9 + Ablakok always; the rest only when the layer has such items
opts.d: Compact; nothing hidden that has content.
Shortest, but rows appear and disappear.
0 % is what the eye button is for.

questions.q: What does 'link layers' mean in the Planner?
questions.why: Photoshop links move together; the Planner has no whole-layer move.

opts.t: A + a 'move linked layers' offset tool
opts.d: Adds whole-layer moving (new feature, more work).
Linked layers merge when the stack is finalised.

opts.t: Merge into a chosen target only

questions.q: Duplicate a layer — copy its walls too?
questions.why: A copied wall lies exactly on the original; walls merge visually.

opts.t: Off by default, checkbox to include

questions.q: Add a layer lock (not in the draft)?
questions.why: Marking on top of a construction layer invites accidental wall drags.

opts.t: Yes — locked items draw and snap but cannot be selected
opts.d: Small, useful for the Szerkezet layer.

sections.title: Marking layer (Wave B)
sections.note: Rules, restrictions and preferences that later layers read.

questions.why: Load-bearing walls are a hard 'no', not just 'avoid'.

opts.d: Tilos raises warnings on routes and placements.

opts.t: Two: + and − as in the draft

questions.q: Keys for the two marking tools
questions.why: J (jelölés) and G (padló/grid) look free; verified at build time.

opts.t: J = wall tool (J again cycles), G = floor/ceiling tool, Tab = floor↔ceiling
One wall mark per wall per layer; a second click edits it
opts.d: Material is one fact about a wall.

questions.q: Trace end snaps to a door within…

opts.t: 600 mm, end placed 250 mm inside the room

opts.d: Looser — risk of grabbing the wrong door in a corridor.

questions.q: Smoothing for the smoothed freehand mode

opts.d: Removes jitter, keeps the shape, ends fixed.

questions.why: Your description: doors relative to each other, traces on a 500 mm grid around them.

opts.t: Directional by default; grid frame at the start door (u along wall, v into room)

opts.d: → security contact + heating off when open
no boxes below the sill, thermostat away

questions.why: Door, strip and floor/ceiling tag lists are in 01_CATALOGUES §3 — edit them freely.

questions.q: What is a BRIDGE Stack in the data?

opts.t: Ordinary layers with a role, grouped
opts.d: Every existing tool works on every stack layer.

opts.t: One special layer with internal sub-layers
opts.d: Closer to 'a special layer type', but every tool needs teaching.

questions.q: When a stack is active, the left stage rail…

opts.d: '◂ Általános' returns to the normal stages.

opts.t: …stays; the stack gets its own panel

questions.q: Using existing layers in a new stack

opts.t: Reference them (they join the stack); several can be merged first

opts.d: Originals untouched; two copies of the walls.

questions.q: Rooms from the building model have no stable id

opts.d: Invisible to you; marks and RBX assignments can point at them.

opts.t: Require converting them to drawn floors

questions.q: Order of the phase-2 system layers
questions.why: Your draft starts with the simplest and puts SECURITY last.

opts.t: BRIDGE build order: Erősáram, A busz, B busz, Vezérlés, Adat, (KNX), Érzékelők, Rádió, Kezelők, Média, USB, Biztonság
opts.d: STD-001 §6; every step needs nothing from a later one.

questions.q: Which rooms does a newly placed RBX serve automatically?

opts.t: The room it faces + the room behind its wall

opts.d: Moving a room to another box asks.

opts.t: Multi-wall model: distance + loss per wall, from your wall tags
opts.d: Tartófal costs more than gipszkarton. Typical values, editable.

opts.t: One device per placed group, units = any of NET/COMP/MEDIA
opts.d: Whole BASE = one device; split = up to three.

opts.t: Derived from the two end types (BASE–RBX = CHANNEL bundle, board–RBX = room circuits…), overridable

questions.q: Chained RoomBox: the upstream bundle carries downstream rooms' uplinks — C1 M25 holds two Cat6A
questions.why: STD-001 fixes the bundle sizes but does not say what a chain does. This is a gap in the standard, found while specifying the fill.

opts.t: Fill as specified and warn on overfill
opts.d: Decide case by case; nothing silent.

opts.t: A second, parallel bundle per chained room

opts.d: Breaks the 'fixed sizes' rule of STD-001 §3.1.

opts.t: Soft — badges and hints, never blocks
opts.d: You decide when to move on.

opts.t: Hard — next layer locked until the previous is done
From the room name (konyha, fürdő…), overridable per room

questions.why: Manual-first: the switch is an input to the RoomBox's bistable; lamps are outputs. No switch-to-lamp wire.

opts.t: Switch = input (own run to RBX), lamp groups by 'what does this switch control' — default 230 V pushbutton

opts.d: That is wiring-pipeline S6 — a separate, later job.

opts.t: Sockets and lamp groups daisy-chained, KNX a line, everything else a home run
opts.d: Steiner tree kept for future 'tree' cases.

questions.q: Six new type codes for STD-004
questions.why: No code exists for these: DED big load, ETH data outlet, SCR screen, AVP AV position, USB data point, SEC security point.

opts.d: Write the names in the note.

opts.t: Replace the automatic result, never touch manual edits (flag them when stale)

questions.why: A cable can only leave its conduit at a box.

opts.t: One pipe per run leg; same family between the same two boxes share
opts.d: Physically exact; more small pipes side by side.

opts.t: Merge same-family cables on shared segments
opts.d: Fewer pipes, but needs a box at every branch.

opts.t: Route length + 0.5 m per end + waste % from settings, labelled tájékoztató

questions.q: Room-circuit feed to a RoomBox: pipe packing
questions.why: STD-001 says M25 per circuit group; A2 says two S04 circuits → M32.

opts.t: Pack up to M32, minimum M25 per pipe

opts.d: One earth fault trips one circuit.

opts.t: Greedy by typical kW, hob split over two phases

questions.q: Stack view ('draw on the stack as one layer')

opts.t: All stack layers shown, other layers faded to 30 %
